Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. We put together a compact commercial worksheet and a recommended pilot path that aligns with enterprise procurement templates. High level answers below; attached is a downloadable SKU matrix and the proposed SOW.

- Retention scoping: We support both account-wide and project/namespace-level retention. For AegisHealth I recommend per-project buckets (three buckets) so you can allocate storage credits and apply different SLA tiers per stack. That avoids cross-subsidization across teams.

- Tracing pricing: We price on ingest + retained-span volume. For sampled traces we apply a lower ingest multiplier and a tiered retention fee; full-span retention is higher. For ~2K RPS peak, our recommended default is 2% sampling for hot-path + 0.1% for full-trace snapshots (we included a cost simulation in the worksheet).

- Bundles & discounts: For a 12-month commit across all three add-ons we can offer a blended discount that increases with committed spend. Example: 10% at $150k ARR, 15% at $300k ARR, with a demo-credit & onboarding waiver at the larger commit. The attached matrix lays out examples and the seat-equivalent conversions.

Pilot/demo-credit suggestion: 6 weeks technical pilot, $25k in demo/ingest credits (applies to retention & tracing), and one-time onboarding waiver for advanced dashboards. If Procurement needs a smaller pilot, we can scale the credit down and offer an extended proof-of-value with a consumption cap.

Next steps: I've attached the SKU matrix (Aegis_OBS_SKU_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a proposed SOW (proposed-SOW-obs-addons.pdf). Can you confirm which procurement template they need the worksheet in (we can convert), and whether Procurement expects a redline-friendly term sheet or a full purchase order?

If it helps, Ben and Laura are looped for commercial concessions and SOW/implementation scoping. Happy to jump on a 30-min call Thurs or Fri.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Laura / Ben — forwarding Emma's latest. Procurement is asking for written sequencing and explicit waiver language. My proposal below (to send as a one-page commercial summary):

- Pilot mechanics: 6-week pilot, $25k demo/ingest credits (applied as a prepayment credit). If customer converts to a 12-month commit at or above $200k ARR, the credit is treated as an advance and reduces year-one invoiced ARR (i.e., applied against the first invoice). If commit is < $200k but >= $125k, credit is firmed as a one-time concession (no ARR reduction).

- Discount tiering:
  * Tier A: $125k-199k ARR -> 10% blended discount + onboarding waiver (standard remote onboarding).
  * Tier B: $200k-399k ARR -> 15% blended discount + onboarding waiver + two onsite workshops (travel expenses billed).
  * Tier C: >= $400k ARR -> 20% blended discount + onboarding waiver + SLA uplift (99.95% retention archive SLA) and dedicated TAM hours (quarterly).

- Onboarding waiver (explicit): covers data pipeline review up to 40 engineering hours, dashboard template import (up to 10 templates), and two remote training sessions. Onsite workshops included only for Tier B and above (travel reimbursed).

- SLA uplift: Eligible at Tier C only. SLA uptime availability for archival reads and writes to be set at 99.95% with an extended credit schedule in the SOW (we should draft the exact credit table for legal).

I recommend the one-page commercial summary (PDF) include the above bullet points + example invoice treatment and a redline-friendly clause for the credit application. Ben — can you confirm margin impact if we treat pilot credit as ARR reduction at the $200k threshold (vs concession)? Laura — can you draft a concise waiver paragraph we can hand to Procurement?

If you both sign off, I'll send this to Emma with the one-page summary and attach the SOW draft for legal redline.

Thanks,
Karthik
